title: Collapse directive taxonomy to blocking required advisory
description: WHY: the current taxonomy is severity (info, action, required, blocking) times kind (obligation, next_step, warning, recovery, summary, acknowledgement) times lifecycle (proposed, active, satisfied, acknowledged, superseded, blocked) times lane (informational, recommended, required, blocked) - a combinatorial space where most cells change no consumer behavior. Lane is already derived from severity in ui-model (packages/ui-model/src/work-view.ts lines 30-31 and the lane mapping); lifecycle mostly mirrors gate status. WHAT: collapse to a single severity of blocking, required or advisory; keep kind only if at least one consumer branches on it (audit consumers first - apps/cli directive formatting, apps/console, ui-model WorkDirectiveSummaryView lines 89-105); drop lifecycle from the bundle (gap presence is liveness - a satisfied gap simply stops being emitted). Update the JSON schema, the ui-model views and lanes, and the directive-acknowledgement record references (packages/core/src/records.ts lines 236-267) as needed. Record the cut as a decision note since this changes a published schema.
acceptanceCriteria: Bundle schema exposes exactly blocking, required and advisory severities with a decision note recording the cut
ui-model, CLI text formatting, console and MCP render the collapsed taxonomy with tests passing
No consumer branches on a removed enum value, verified by grep and compile
closedReason: Directive taxonomy collapse complete with verified tests; Git checkpoint blocked by sandbox index write restriction
